title: ChipAgents Accelerates Chip Design With Agentic Physics-Aware Models
author: Daniel Nenni
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Summary:
ChipAgents is targeting the physical AI market with a full-stack automation platform designed to accelerate digital and analog chip development. The startup's IC-Star engine utilizes physics-aware models, a reasoning core, an IC design ontology, and a design-driven model navigator to handle complex workflows. Rising chip complexity currently results in only ten percent of designs working on the first tapeout, creating an unsustainable situation for the semiconductor industry. Early-access customers such as Andes Technology, eMemory, and WhaleChip have already realized significant efficiency gains and time reductions using the technology. Furthermore, Rambus is adopting the platform to help customers bring advanced chips to market faster.

Using AI to speed chip design has become a hot topic of late! AI models can be used to do for chips what Anthropic has done for software: speed up the work so you can do more work. After providing some perspective on three startups, I recently covered what Cognichip and Cadence design has announced, and now another company has announced new chip-design AI, targeting both digital and analog chips: ChipAgents.

ChipAgents Is Targeting the Vast Physical AI Chip Design Market
While data center growth is currently consuming everyone’s attention, Physical AI is touted as the next big thing in AI, bringing robotic intelligence and automated vehicles to market. Unfortunately, this vision has a rather large problem: the current industry cannot possibly provide the number of chip designs needed to populate the vast array of physical devices envisioned. ChipAgents, a startup I covered in my overview of three startups driving Agentic AI solutions to accelerate chip development, has estimated that each physical AI device could consist of upwards of 3000 chips. Sounds high to me, but when you do the math at a projected 145 million devices, that implies some half trillion chips could be required from the semiconductor industry, an impossibility given then current capacity for chip design and production. Even if the 3000 number is too high, the industry will undoubtedly need a lot of chips; a good market to target for automation.

Are We There Yet?
Have we reached fully autonomous chip design? No, chip design still requires a design team with full knowledge of the problem to be solved, the unique approach to solve it, and expertise honed by years of design experiences. But an AI that is rooted in physics and design experience can help the design team’s junior engineers perform at a higher level, and hopefully allow the senior engineers focus on the magic that leads to competitive advantage.
